column1: # Adjudication of every CFTypeID CoreFoundation defines.
# Checked by scripts/check_registration.py, which REFUSES if any typeID CF
# defines is missing here, if a row names a typeID CF does not define, or if
# a verdict contradicts CF's own dispatch sites. This file adjudicates; it
# cannot invent membership -- the BRIDGED set is derived from CF's source and
# the checker fails on disagreement in either direction.
# BRIDGED means CF dispatches on the type: it appears as the first argument of
# CF_IS_OBJC or CF_OBJC_[RETAINED_]FUNCDISPATCHV, so CF is prepared to receive a
# foreign ObjC instance of it and MUST be able to tell one from its own struct.
# The class names are a SPECIFICATION OF WHAT WE WILL IMPLEMENT, not a claim
# about Apple's. Three are attested in corelibs' own source, via
# INIT_CFRUNTIME_BASE_WITH_CLASS(CLASS, TYPEID) in CFNumber.c and CFBase.c:
# follow CF's own __NSCF<Type> convention. None of them exist yet, which is why
# the checker currently reports MISSING_CLASS for all 19 -- that is the honest
# state, and the list doubles as the work order for the NS* implementations.
# Two BRIDGED types are dispatched but never MESSAGED: CFBag's three sites
# (CFBag.c:250,258,266) are "if ObjC, bail" guards that return 0/false. They
# still need a registered class so the predicate answers correctly; they do not
# need a method surface. CFBoolean is the same shape.
# NOT_BRIDGED types are safe to leave unregistered: _CFRuntimeCreateInstance
# initialises _cfisa from the very slot CF_IS_OBJC compares against
# (CFRuntime.c:550), so an unregistered type's own instances match their own
# empty slot and read as native, correctly.
